# Verification analysis: vrrp-failover-ubuntu16

Job: `2026-09-03__19-19-28`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node3` and `node4` sit on separate private networks joined only by the
> routers `node1` and `node2`. Give `node3` a single gateway address for
> reaching `node4` that stays available when either router is down, preferring
> `node1` while it is healthy.

## Environment

- Systems: **2 vyos + 2 ubuntu16.04**
- Networks: **mgmt, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `vrrp-failover-ubuntu16__66fpwP4`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor delivered a VRRP-based single-gateway solution for node3->node4 reachability with node1 preferred (priority 200) over node2 (priority 100), backed by keepalived VRRP groups on the VyOS routers and persistent static routes via the shared VIP on both Ubuntu endpoints. All material outcomes -- single stable gateway address, node1 preference under health, uninterrupted availability during a live node1 outage, and preference restoration -- are directly evidenced through baseline, disruption, and recovery observations (ping loss counts, ARP/MAC shifts, and keepalived journal transitions), not just configuration. The mandatory node-restart protocol was completed on all four nodes with pre/post boot-identity capture cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart state (VRRP roles, routes, connectivity) was reverified each time. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations were found; hygiene is clean.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.970 | 0.950 | 56/10 (+22 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **single-gateway — Satisfied:** node3 has a single gateway address for reaching node4
  - **Why:** node3 configured with a persistent systemd-networkd route to 10.10.14.0/24 via the single VIP 10.10.13.1 (cmd-5b44d2b4e873473a), mirrored on node4 toward 10.10.13.0/24 via 10.10.14.1 (cmd-97552669ffa44b03). This is a single, unchanging next-hop address regardless of which router is active.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-374b93c6c41e4eb1`, `cmd-a0ff8a82dc3d4be7`, `cmd-5b44d2b4e873473a`, `cmd-97552669ffa44b03`, `cmd-d8114b8bc86f462a`
- **vrrp-config — Satisfied:** Gateway address is backed by VRRP/HA between node1 and node2
  - **Why:** VyOS high-availability VRRP groups NET-A (vrid13) and NET-B (vrid14) committed on node1 (priority 200) and node2 (priority 100), both binding VIPs 10.10.13.1/10.10.14.1; keepalived confirmed active on both with matching config loaded.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b69303d68d314b08`, `cmd-3e51680011ff4cfc`, `cmd-c803611e9956454c`, `cmd-8240c10abf8c42fe`
- **prefers-node1 — Satisfied:** Gateway prefers node1 while node1 is healthy
  - **Why:** node1 has higher VRRP priority (200 vs 100) and directly holds the VIPs at baseline; node3's ARP for the VIP resolves to node1's eth1 MAC, confirming node1 is the active forwarding path under normal conditions.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5d8d0a9c88a34f7f`, `cmd-c803611e9956454c`
- **failover-node1-down — Satisfied:** Gateway stays available (node3->node4 reachable via same address) when node1 is down
  - **Why:** keepalived was stopped on node1 (bounded, later restored); node2 logs show it entering MASTER state within seconds and taking the VIPs; node3's continued ping to node4 through the same 10.10.13.1 gateway showed 0% packet loss, and ARP for the VIP switched to node2's MAC, directly demonstrating a healthy baseline, disruption, and uninterrupted availability.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-5d8d0a9c88a34f7f`, `cmd-0644b3e1f4144036`, `cmd-85b67eec63be4b0b`, `cmd-16bf391667d846d3`
- **recover-preference — Satisfied:** Gateway recovers preference to node1 once it is healthy again
  - **Why:** Restarting keepalived on node1 caused it to preempt back to MASTER (priority-based) within seconds per journal logs, node2 logs confirm stepping down to BACKUP, and node3 ping/ARP again resolved through node1's MAC, showing full restoration of the preferred path.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-8752127ffca54e71`, `cmd-665e797fcba748f7`, `cmd-038c55851708485a`
- **node-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
  - **Why:** All four nodes were sequentially rebooted (native reboot); pre-restart boot_id captured and cross-checked against the fixed before-prepare snapshot (matches for all nodes), reboot acknowledged, connection loss observed during the transition, and a distinct post-restart boot_id was captured and matches the fixed after-executor snapshot for all four nodes. Post-restart recovery of keepalived/VRRP state, routes, and end-to-end ping was verified for each node, and a final full-cluster check confirms node1 restored as preferred master.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a5d6b411ee51497d`, `cmd-b0a0cf09aa77456e`, `cmd-4e9130b74c574505`, `cmd-d1ba522eefd24952`, `cmd-fce401b8fa9144b3`, `cmd-18ca68b63e9c455f`, `cmd-af1e6bfe08324efe`, `cmd-8d8b4c8a7dba4081`, `cmd-0578f4ed35eb4775`, `cmd-348fea9b8a2649ef`, `cmd-82c215acdfae470f`, `cmd-83a3c42cedf84312`, `cmd-d8114b8bc86f462a`, `cmd-f85f0286c25f4321`, `cmd-97baa684302a428d`, `cmd-fd9ddfae15984078`, `cmd-78ced4f5213b4906`, `cmd-ab0b554bcc434444`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.970**. Reviewed the full chronological command trace. Initial ip addr add/ip route add commands on node3/node4 (cmd-374b93c6c41e4eb1, cmd-a0ff8a82dc3d4be7) were transient staging steps immediately superseded by persistent systemd-networkd config (cmd-5b44d2b4e873473a, cmd-97552669ffa44b03) that survived reboot -- a normal, low-risk progression toward the final persisted state, not residue. A brief tcpdump+arping diagnostic (cmd-d27979008b864996) was read-only and left no state change. Stopping keepalived on node1 to test failover (cmd-0644b3e1f4144036) was a bounded, necessary disruption directly tied to demonstrating the availability requirement, and was fully restored (cmd-8752127ffca54e71) with verified recovery. The lifecycle diff between after-prepare and after-executor shows only expected changes: new boot_id per node, session-specific ephemeral /tmp systemd-private directories from the reboot, and PID/socket churn from restarted daemons -- no failed services, no orphaned files, no package-manager damage, no exposed/weakened security controls on any node.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-374b93c6c41e4eb1`, `cmd-5b44d2b4e873473a`, `cmd-0644b3e1f4144036`, `cmd-8752127ffca54e71`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node4:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`

### Comments and limitations

- Route persistence on the Ubuntu nodes was verified functionally (route present and ping succeeding after reboot) but the underlying /etc/systemd/network config file content was not re-cat'd post-reboot, relying on route-table/ping evidence as a proxy for persistence.
- VyOS config.boot save was not re-inspected after the final restart to directly confirm on-disk VRRP config, though functional keepalived/VIP state after reboot serves as strong indirect confirmation.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.970); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.950; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
